clue.text: Shirts lost here. Desire, after all, loses one in laundry

indicators.note: the laundry word is wrapped around the rest, which sits in it

parts.note: laundry is the wash, the clothes to be washed

indicators.note: after places the desire word behind the word all in the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: loses means the desire word drops the letter named as one

parts.note: A Streetcar Named Desire, the Tennessee Williams play, so a desire is a streetcar
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A grumble about a laundry that keeps losing shirts, with desire somehow part of the washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire' is the streetcar of Tennessee Williams's play, and 'loses one' drops its A. To 'lose your shirt' is to lose everything, as investors did in the 1929 crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's shirt is an idiom for financial ruin, and the 1929 stock market collapse is where many investors were ruined.

clue.text: The town crier is running late

definitions.text: The town crier is running late

parts.words: The town crier is running late
parts.note: not a herald with a bell but the nursery-rhyme boy who runs through the town at night in his nightgown, crying at the windows that it is past eight o'clock

explanation.surface: An official town crier is behind schedule for his announcements.
explanation.walkthrough: A town crier is normally a civic official; here it is the nursery-rhyme child who runs through the town crying at windows and locks late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme describes this character running through the town after eight o'clock, crying through the locks.

clue.text: Sinister cult has locked up its riches

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the captured letters are read from bottom to top
the phrase has locked means the letters are held inside the words Sinister cult

explanation.surface: A sinister cult hoards its wealth behind locked doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has locked' takes ERCUL from sinistER CULt and 'up' turns it round in this down entry; 'its' is a link word tying the riches to the cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or wealth, usually with a sense of greed, as in the phrase filthy lucre.

clue.text: Someone in a restaurant in Cornwall or Jersey

parts.note: Cornwall is in the far south-west of England, abbreviated SW
a diner in a restaurant is an eater

explanation.surface: Looking for a diner somewhere in Cornwall or on Jersey, two holiday spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the Channel Island paired with Cornwall as a place, but it is the knitted garment. SW is the South West, the region of England where Cornwall lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted pullover, the same garment as a sweater.

clue.text: Outwardly profligate young man filling in with this?

indicators.note: outwardly means the profligate word goes on the outside, around the young man

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute, profligate man
a young man is a lad

explanation.surface: A dissolute playboy surrounds a youth, and asks whether to fill in with this.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: a roulade is a dish rolled up around a filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled dish of meat, sponge or pastry wrapped around a filling.

clue.text: Encourage head to drop towards feet of clay …

indicators.note: the word's head letter sinks from the top toward the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: to encourage is to hearten
the head is the first letter of the encouraging word

explanation.surface: Telling someone to cheer up and look down towards their feet of clay.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue but does no work. 'Feet of clay' is a hidden flaw; here 'of clay' is the definition, and HEARTEN's H drops towards the foot of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen describes something made of baked clay, such as earthenware pots.

clue.text: … worker on coverings for feet left aiming for head dress

indicators.note: the letter for left moves up toward the head of the word in this down entry

parts.note: a cobbler mends shoes, the coverings for feet

explanation.surface: A shoemaker heads off, aiming to dress up.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of COBBLER moves up toward the front of the word. 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes or gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British slang for clothes, so to clobber someone can also mean to dress them.

clue.text: In compiling, Afrit (without love) or Enigmatist (with stronger reason)

indicators.note: compiling puts letters together afresh, so the gathered letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written; Afrit was the pseudonym of the setter A. F. Ritchie
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
taken as written
the setter of this puzzle refers to himself, so Enigmatist is I

explanation.surface: Two crossword compilers compared, the old master without love and the current setter with stronger reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Afrit was a famous Listener setter; 'without' just sets the O beside him. Enigmatist is this puzzle's setter, so he is I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in argument to mean all the more so, for an even stronger reason.

clue.text: Sporting myth — viewer has to be treated with a "V"

definitions.text: Sporting myth — viewer has to be treated with a "V"

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the listed letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sporting legend that a television viewer has to be shown a V sign.
explanation.walkthrough: Show jumper Harvey Smith made a V sign at the judges in 1971, and the gesture took his name; the whole clue both describes it and supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-fingered insulting gesture is named after a British show jumper who famously made it at a competition.

clue.text: What, some Europeans say, old singer's got in purse

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: got in means the European word is taken inside the singer's name

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
que is the French and Spanish word for what

explanation.surface: Speculating on what some old singer has in her purse.
explanation.walkthrough: The purse here is the national treasury, not a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: The national purse is a name for public funds, which are managed by the government's finance department.

clue.text: The Guardian's about to make a stink

indicators.note: about means the newspaper's word goes around the word for make

parts.note: The Guardian, the newspaper setting the puzzle, speaks of itself as ours
to make is to do

explanation.surface: The newspaper is about to kick up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To make a stink' reads as causing a fuss, but 'make' is wordplay and the definition is the noun stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink is a strong smell, which is an odour in its unpleasant sense.

clue.text: Top wine waiter's pointless and muddled, showing sluggishness

indicators.note: muddled means the remaining letters are jumbled
pointless means the compass points W and E are taken away
top means the first letter of the phrase is lopped off

parts.note: the phrase is used as written

explanation.surface: The head sommelier has lost his edge and is confused and slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' removes the first W of WINEWAITER; 'pointless' takes out a further W and E, compass points, leaving INAITER, which 'muddled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay still or do nothing, which is a state of lethargy.

clue.text: One of the regulars is rather noticeable in appearance

indicators.note: noticeable in says the rather word can be seen within the appearance word

parts.note: a hue is a colour or aspect, an appearance
rather means a bit, somewhat

explanation.surface: A regular customer stands out a little in the way they look.
explanation.walkthrough: A BIT ('rather') sits inside HUE ('appearance').
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means a regular visitor to a place such as a bar or club.

clue.text: What's owed penniless victim of trickery

indicators.note: penniless means the letter P, a penny, is removed

parts.note: a dupe is someone fooled or tricked

explanation.surface: Money owed to someone conned and left broke.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money.
explanation.definitionFit: What is owed is a debt that is payable, so it is due.

clue.text: Plant polled fern included in enigmatic clue

indicators.note: included in means the trimmed plant word goes within the reworked clue letters
enigmatic means puzzling, so the letters of clue are jumbled
polled means beheaded, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fern turning up in a puzzling crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enigmatic' turns CLUE into LUCE; 'polled' (with its head cut off) turns FERN into ERN, which is 'included in' LUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a fodder plant, also known as alfalfa.

clue.text: The fourth described thus by poet in case change to 2 takes precedence

definitions.text: The fourth described thus by poet

indicators.note: takes precedence means the rearranged piece comes first, ahead of the in case word
change to means the letters of the answer to clue 2 are rearranged

parts.note: refers to the answer to 2 down
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A poet describing the fourth item, with a change to number two taking priority.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourth is April, the fourth month; T. S. Eliot opens The Waste Land with 'April is the cruellest month'. The anagram of 2's answer goes before LEST.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot called April, the fourth month, the most unkind of months in the opening line of The Waste Land.

clue.text: Footballer's reciprocal love for tennis player

definitions.text: Footballer's reciprocal love for tennis player

parts.words: Footballer's reciprocal love for tennis player
parts.note: a zero score is love in tennis, so the footballer's word that corresponds to it is the football term for nothing

explanation.surface: A footballer's romance with a tennis player is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a sporting romance, but 'love' is the tennis score of zero and the footballer's matching word is the football term for no goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Football scores give zero as this word, just as tennis calls it love.

clue.text: Jumpy over spread in back of tabloid

indicators.note: in means the spread letters go inside the turned tabloid name
back of means the tabloid's name is read backwards

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: spread means the letters of over are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone edgy about a centre-page spread at the back of a tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' is the anagram signal and 'back of' turns the tabloid round. The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervous means being anxious and on edge, much like feeling jumpy.

clue.text: One sees part of rare object in haystack

definitions.meaning: an organ of sight, something one sees with

definitions.text: part of rare object in haystack
definitions.meaning: a needle in a haystack is famously rare to find, and part of a needle is the hole for the thread

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fragment of a rare object lost in a haystack.
explanation.walkthrough: The rare object is the proverbial needle in a haystack, and the hole in its top has the same name as the organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ of sight shares its name with the hole in a needle through which thread passes.

clue.text: Even Pequod's missing circling whales with competence

indicators.note: missing circling means the letters wrapped around the middle of the ship's name are taken away

parts.note: the Pequod is Captain Ahab's whaling ship in Moby-Dick
a pod is a group of whales
able means competent

explanation.surface: The whaling ship Pequod is missing the whales it was circling, though handled competently.
explanation.walkthrough: The whales sit around the middle of the ship's name, which is why the clue says 'circling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Equable means even-tempered and steady, never extreme.

clue.text: Two reports of money being integral to the deal

indicators.note: two reports means two spoken words, each matching a word for money

parts.note: a bill is a banknote and tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Money is an essential part of the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: BILL (a banknote) and TIN (old slang for money) said together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built in is included as an integral part of the package.

clue.text: Bucolics, say, turn up to feed drug to pointer

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: to feed means the turned word goes into the pointer word

parts.note: a clue is a pointer, a hint

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Instructions for drugging a pointer dog in a pastoral poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GO into OG, which goes 'to feed' into CLUE; E is the drug ecstasy. Virgil's Bucolics are better known as his Eclogues.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's Bucolics is a collection of short pastoral poems, each one an example of the form.

clue.text: I long to leave capital before getting occupancy of new sculptor

indicators.note: to leave says the long letter must go from the capital
getting occupancy of means the new letter moves into the vacated spot

parts.note: Berlin is the German capital
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone longing to leave the capital before moving into a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' and 'getting occupancy of' swap N in for L, and I follows. Gian Lorenzo Bernini was the great Baroque sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini was the great Italian Baroque artist who carved many of Rome's statues and fountains.

clue.text: Well done, Bill! Cracking display!

indicators.note: cracking means the bill word breaks into the well done word

parts.note: bravo is a cry of well done
an ad, an advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: Applause for someone called Bill after a superb performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name, but it is AD, a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness, a swaggering display meant to impress.

clue.text: Take to be French and notice the patch-up job

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
et is French for and
to notice something written is to read it

explanation.surface: Thinking a repair is French, and noticing what the botched work is.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'take' comes from the Latin recipe at the head of prescriptions. A retread is a tyre given a new tread, so a patched-up thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is a worn tyre with a fresh tread put on, so a repair or reworking of something old.

clue.text: This vehicle reverses into its club

indicators.note: reverses into means the club's letters run backwards to form the vehicle

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A motorist backs into the clubhouse of their motoring club.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation, so it is the vehicle's own club.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle, the kind the club serves.

clue.text: To demonstrate hostility I shall repeatedly hug women

indicators.note: hug means the doubled word wraps around the women letter
repeatedly means the contraction is used twice

parts.note: I shall contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: To show they are hostile, someone keeps saying they will embrace the women.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL, said twice, with W ('women') between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is malice or animosity felt toward someone.

clue.text: Syrian city not prepared to support MacAllistair's enlightenment?

parts.note: someone anti something is against it, not prepared to back it
och is a Scottish exclamation, here the cry of someone with a Scottish name who suddenly understands

explanation.surface: A Syrian city unwilling to back a Scotsman's moment of insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' looks like placing one piece below another, but it belongs to the phrase meaning anti. Antioch was a major city of ancient Syria, now in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a great city of ancient Syria, founded by one of Alexander's generals.

clue.text: Order — I've found it in Nebraska!

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
aha is a cry of discovery

explanation.surface: Someone receives an honour and shouts with delight on finding something in Nebraska.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city located in the American state of Nebraska.

clue.text: In homage, went down pathetically like 10 that's unnecessary

indicators.note: pathetically means feebly or badly, so the letters are jumbled
unnecessary means the that's letters can be dropped

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. stands for id est, that is
the number ten spelt out

explanation.surface: Someone bowed down in homage, as pitifully as a pointless stink.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to the clue for ODOUR but is just the number TEN. LIKE with IE dropped as 'unnecessary' gives LK, and 'pathetically' mixes LK and TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneel is to go down on one's knees, as subjects did before a monarch in homage.

clue.text: A conventional US vessel for pulling back round a country

indicators.note: round means the towing vessel goes around the second a
back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
in American slang lame means dull and square, conventional
a tug is a boat that tows other vessels

explanation.surface: A traditional American towboat heads back around a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts the second A inside the towing vessel, and 'back' turns the whole run. 'Lame' is American slang for uncool, square.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a republic in Central America, bordering Mexico.

clue.text: Understanding needed to encode a letter in translation?

indicators.note: a translation renders the words in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An understanding is needed to code a letter for translation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1904 agreement between Britain and France is the classic diplomatic understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a friendly understanding between nations, especially the 1904 accord between Britain and France.
